status_reason: The enquiry calls the sample both clear and black, and the UV-Vis transmission concept is blocked for opaque samples, so probe and fiber choice depend on the optical state that is still unknown.
answer: UV-Vis transmission with a 10 mm path cannot be the first in-line method if the crude is black, because transmission saturates in opaque media. The first step is to resolve the clear-versus-black contradiction. The supplied water-in-petroleum example uses MIR ATR absorbance at 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 µm) for 0.1-2.0 % water, so MIR ATR is the method to test first in the laboratory.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR with a ZrO2-tip probe on laboratory water-in-oil samples before any in-line UV-Vis transmission.
inline.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 tip sealed in a PEEK shaft
inline.install: In the pipe only after the optical state and process conditions are confirmed; laboratory test first.
inline.fiber: Chalcogenide As-S (CIR), 1.1-6.5 µm; covers the 2.5-5 µm test range, whereas PIR (3-17 µm) does not reach 2.5 µm.
inline.test_against: UV-ATR probe on the same samples
inline.not_final_because: The sample optical state is contradictory, pipe conditions and spectrometer distance are unknown, and the cited example covers only 0.1-2.0 % water, not the 3 % in the enquiry.

problems.text: The enquiry calls the sample both clear and black or opaque. Clear and opaque samples need different measurement geometries, so the optical state must be confirmed before a probe is chosen.
UV-Vis transmission over a 10 mm path saturates when the sample is opaque, because light cannot penetrate the bulk of black crude. For black crude this concept is blocked.
UV-Vis has low selectivity and overlapping signals, so a water reading would need chemometrics. The supplied water-in-petroleum example uses MIR ATR, not UV-Vis.
The enquiry goes up to 3 % water, but the cited petroleum example shows only 0.1 to 2.0 %, so the range above 2 % needs its own reference samples.

methods.why: Used for water in petroleum with ZrO2 ATR probes, with absorbance rising with water content in the 0.1-2.0 % range shown.
Transmission saturates in opaque oil; a UV-ATR probe is the UV-Vis option for black media, but UV-Vis selectivity is low.
Penetrates several millimetres into dense samples and suits online fiber probes, but its overlapping bands need chemometrics.
Carries information complementary to MIR, but weak signals are often masked by fluorescence from organic compounds.

questions.q: Is the crude clear and light-transmitting, or black and opaque, at the measurement point?
questions.why: This decides whether transmission is possible at all and which probe geometry is used.

questions.q: What are the pipe conditions (temperature, pressure, flow), and can an ATR probe be fitted into the line?
questions.why: The petroleum example gives no process conditions, and probe materials and installation depend on them.

questions.q: How far is the spectrometer from the pipe, in metres?
questions.why: Remote fiber links make the spectrometer independent of the plant floor, and the fiber length affects the choice of fiber.

questions.q: Which water range and accuracy are required, and which independent laboratory method will provide the reference water values?
questions.why: The cited example covers 0.1-2.0 % water only, and reference values must come from independent laboratory analysis.

experiment.objective: Test whether MIR ATR can read water in crude oil across 0-3 % before any in-line installation.
steps: Confirm the optical state of the sample (clear or black) on a sampled batch.
Prepare water-in-oil samples across 0-3 % and measure their water content by an independent laboratory analysis as reference.
Record MIR ATR absorbance spectra over 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 µm) with the ZrO2-tip probe and a chalcogenide As-S fiber.
Build a chemometric model on part of the samples and validate it on held-out samples with segmented cross-validation and randomisation tests.
Run UV-ATR on the same samples as the comparison and keep the method that performs better on the validation set.

pathway.key_features: Absorbance changes with water content in the 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 µm) region, to be confirmed on own samples.
pathway.path_reason: Laboratory trials must first show a water signal and a validated model before a path is chosen.

multispectral.why: Raman carries information complementary to MIR, so it may add information if MIR alone is ambiguous in the laboratory test.
multispectral.test: Build the MIR-only model first; the fused model must beat it on the same held-out samples, otherwise drop Raman.

assumptions: Pipe process conditions (temperature, pressure, flow) are unknown.
The water range is 0-3 % as stated in the enquiry.
The sample optical state is unresolved; both clear and black are possible.
The distance from the pipe to the spectrometer is unknown.
